source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: An ethnographer studying a fishing community tries to understand health practices from the community members' own point of view. This insider perspective is called:
questions.rationale: Ethnographers strive for the emic (insider's) view rather than the etic (outsider's) view.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 11 Summary (PDF p. 286)
questions.quote: Ethnographers strive to acquire an emic (insider’s) perspective of a culture rather than an etic (outsider’s) perspective.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: In descriptive phenomenology, the researcher sets aside her own preconceived views about the experience being studied. This is:
questions.rationale: Bracketing means setting aside preconceptions to remain open to participants' meanings.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 11 Summary (PDF p. 286)
questions.quote: researchers strive to bracket out preconceived views and to intuit the essence of the phenomenon

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: An intensive investigation of one family coping with a member's schizophrenia is a:
questions.rationale: Case studies are intensive investigations of a single entity or a few entities (individuals, families, communities).
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 11 Summary (PDF p. 287)
questions.quote: Case studies are intensive investigations of a single entity or a small number of entities, such as individuals, groups, families, or communities.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Nurses work with an urban poor community to study their water problem and plan collective action together. This approach is:
questions.rationale: PAR produces knowledge through close collaboration with vulnerable groups to motivate action and solidarity.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 11 Summary (PDF p. 287)
questions.quote: Participatory action research(PAR) produces knowledge through close collaboration with groups that are vulnerable to control or oppression

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A researcher studying drug users asks each participant to refer others they know. This sampling method is:
questions.rationale: Snowball (network) sampling uses referrals from earlier participants; useful for hard-to-reach groups.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 12 Summary (PDF p. 305)
questions.quote: Qualitative researchers may start with convenience or snowball sampling

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Phenomenological studies typically involve:
options: A small sample who lived the experience
questions.rationale: Phenomenologists usually work with about 10 or fewer people who have lived the experience.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 12 Summary (PDF p. 306)
questions.quote: Phenomenologists typically work with a small sample of people (often 10 or fewer) who meet the criterion of having lived the experience under study.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: The most widely used data collection method in qualitative studies is:
questions.rationale: In-depth interviews are the most widely used qualitative method, often with observation.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 12 Summary (PDF p. 306)
questions.quote: In-depth interviews are the most widely used method of collecting data for qualitative studies.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A nurse gathers 8 mothers to discuss together their views on child feeding, guided by a moderator. This method is a:
questions.rationale: Focus group interviews involve discussions with small groups on a topic.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 12 Summary (PDF p. 306)
questions.quote: focus group interviews, which involve discussions with small groups

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: An interview that uses a broad topic guide but lets the participant answer freely is:
questions.rationale: Semistructured (focused) interviews use a topic guide; unstructured interviews are conversational.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 12 Summary (PDF p. 306)
questions.quote: semistructured (or focused) interviews, using a broad topic guide

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A researcher joins the daily activities of a home for the aged while observing and recording events in field notes. This is:
questions.rationale: In participant observation, the researcher participates in a group's functioning while observing in depth.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 12 Summary (PDF p. 306)
questions.quote: participant observation, in which the researcher gains entrée into a social group and participates to varying degrees in its functioning

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: In grounded theory, new data are continually compared with earlier data and categories. This is called:
questions.rationale: Grounded theory uses the constant comparative method of analysis.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 11 Summary (PDF p. 286)
questions.quote: Grounded theory uses constant comparison: Categories elicited from the data are constantly compared with data obtained earlier.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: The first step in analyzing qualitative interview transcripts is usually to:
questions.rationale: Qualitative analysis begins by organizing and coding data into categories, then searching for themes.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 16 Summary (PDF p. 410)
questions.quote: A first step in analyzing qualitative data is to organize and index the materials for easy retrieval, typically by coding the content

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Qualitative researchers analyze their data mainly by looking for:
questions.rationale: Qualitative analysis searches for patterns and themes, then weaves them into an integrated picture.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 16 Summary (PDF p. 410)
questions.quote: The actual analysis of data begins with a search for patterns and themes

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Confidence in the truth value of qualitative findings, the counterpart of internal validity, is:
questions.rationale: Lincoln and Guba: credibility ≈ internal validity; dependability ≈ reliability; transferability ≈ external validity; confirmability = objectivity.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 17 Summary (PDF p. 430)
questions.quote: Credibility, which refers to confidence in the truth value of the findings, has been viewed as the qualitative equivalent of internal validity.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: The stability of qualitative data over time and conditions, similar to reliability, is:
questions.rationale: Dependability is somewhat analogous to reliability in quantitative studies.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 17 Summary (PDF p. 431)
questions.quote: Dependability, the stability of data over time and over conditions, is somewhat analogous to reliability in quantitative studies.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Whether qualitative findings can apply to other settings or groups is called:
questions.rationale: Transferability is the qualitative analog of external validity; thick description helps readers judge it.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 17 Summary (PDF p. 431)
questions.quote: Transferability, the analog of external validity, is the extent to which findings can be transferred to other settings or groups.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A researcher shows participants her emerging themes and asks if they reflect their experiences. This strategy is:
questions.rationale: Member checks ask participants to review and react to emerging conceptualizations, enhancing credibility.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 17 Summary (PDF p. 431)
questions.quote: member checks (asking study participants to review and react to emerging conceptualizations)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A qualitative researcher keeps detailed records of every decision and data source so an outside auditor could follow the study. This record is the:
questions.rationale: An audit trail allows an inquiry audit and supports dependability and confirmability.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 17 Summary (PDF p. 431)
questions.quote: comprehensive recording of information (including maintenance of an audit trail)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A researcher stays in the community for many months to understand it fully. This quality strategy is:
questions.rationale: Prolonged engagement aims for adequate scope of data coverage; persistent observation aims for depth.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 17 Summary (PDF p. 431)
questions.quote: prolonged engagement, which strives for adequate scope of data coverage

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A study first surveys 300 nurses about burnout and then interviews 10 of them in depth. This is a:
questions.rationale: Mixed methods research collects, analyzes and integrates both quantitative and qualitative data.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 13 Summary (PDF p. 323)
questions.quote: Mixed methods research involves the collection, analysis, and integration of both quantitative and qualitative data

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: In the structure–process–outcome model of health care quality, nursing skill mix and staffing are examples of:
questions.rationale: Structure = resources and organization; process = nursing actions; outcome = end results for patients.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 13 Summary (PDF p. 324)
questions.quote: structure (e.g., nursing skill mix), process (nursing interventions and actions), and outcomes

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A nursing audit checks whether nurses followed the protocol for IV site care. This evaluates:
questions.rationale: Process refers to the nursing interventions and actions performed.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 13 Summary (PDF p. 324)
questions.quote: process (nursing interventions and actions)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A hospital measures the rate of patient falls and pressure ulcers on its wards. These are:
questions.rationale: Outcomes are the end results of patient care; falls and pressure ulcers are nursing-sensitive outcomes.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 13 Summary (PDF p. 324)
questions.quote: outcomes (the specific end results of patient care in terms of patient functioning)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Research that assesses how well a program, policy or procedure works to help decision makers is:
questions.rationale: Evaluation research assesses the effectiveness of programs or policies to guide decisions.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 13 Summary (PDF p. 324)
questions.quote: Evaluation research assesses the effectiveness of a program, policy, or procedure to assist decision makers in choosing a course of action.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Research that asks people about their characteristics, behaviors and opinions through questionnaires or interviews is:
questions.rationale: Surveys may use face-to-face or telephone interviews or self-administered questionnaires.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 13 Summary (PDF p. 324)
questions.quote: Survey research examines people’s characteristics, behaviors, intentions, and opinions by asking them to answer questions.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: In a clinical trial, the full experimental test of an intervention's efficacy with randomization occurs in:
questions.rationale: Phase I finalizes the intervention, II gives preliminary evidence, III is the full experimental test, IV studies effectiveness in practice.
questions.source: Polit & Beck, Essentials of Nursing Research, 9th ed. (2018), Ch. 13 Summary (PDF p. 324)
questions.quote: Phase III is a full experimental test of treatment efficacy.
